findings.summary: Private retry wrapper can be deleted without changing behavior.
findings.consequence: The method adds an extra indirection for a two-step operation that is used only once, while identical retry composition is still spelled out at other failure sites, so it does not centralize the retry policy or reduce complexity.
findings.evidence: `#retryBatch` only calls `#requeueFront(batch)` and `#scheduleRetry()`. `rg` shows its only call is the normal delivery failure path at line 577, while the same two calls are written directly in exit failure paths at lines 423-424 and 626-627.
findings.recommendation: Delete `#retryBatch` and replace its only call with `this.#requeueFront(batch); this.#scheduleRetry();`, or make all retry failure paths use one helper if the intent is centralization.
